report.source_text: Two weeks later, the patient underwent thoracoscopic resection of the left lung cancer. Macroscopic examination revealed that the excised 14×9.5×3.5-cm upper left lobe included a 3.1×2.5×2-cm mass with gray and grayish black sections, solid, medium in texture, and indistinct from the surrounding boundary (Fig. 3). The mass was adjacent to the pleura and did not involve the bronchus. Histologically, the tumor cells were moderately to poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the acinar and micropapillary type (Fig. 4A-D), and no cryptococcal infection was observed. No metastatic cancer was found in the lymph nodes (0/11), the bronchial incisive margin was negative and the pathological TNM stage was T2aN0Mx.

report.source_text: Within five years after the resection, the patient was admitted to the respiratory department of our hospital regularly for further follow-up (every 6 months for the first 2 years and once a year for the last 3 years), and the latest follow-up was in August 2023. The patient was in good condition and contrast-enhanced CT showed no recurrence of either disease (Fig. 1B, C, E and F).

clinician.final_diagnosis: Pulmonary cryptococcal infection confirmed by CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy with histopathology and special fungal stains
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 65-year-old woman with no symptoms was found by routine chest CT to have two lung nodules suspicious for malignancy. One nodule in the posterior basal segment of the left lower lobe was biopsied under CT guidance. Histopathology revealed granulomatous inflammation with yeast-form fungi, and cryptococcus was identified using PAS, GMS, and mucicarmine stains, confirming pulmonary cryptococcal infection. Concurrently, the anterior segment nodule in the left upper lobe was resected thoracoscopically and diagnosed as primary lung adenocarcinoma. Post-surgery, the patient was treated with fluconazole 200 mg/day for 6 months. Over 5 years of follow-up with regular imaging, no recurrence of cryptococcosis or lung cancer was observed, and the patient remained in good condition.
